transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-17
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Emma Ruiz (Acero Head of ML), Sam Carter (SRE), Liam O'Neill (Product), Nora Zhang (Data Eng), Alex Park (Security)

Summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on model catalog comparison and pinning strategy. Discussed metrics from last run, tradeoffs (latency vs cost), and next steps for canary + fallback testing.

00:00 Jordan: Alright, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
00:06 Emma: Emma here.
00:07 Sam: Sam, yep.
00:09 Liam: Liam.
00:10 Nora: Nora.
00:11 Alex: Alex on security.
00:13 Jordan: Great. Priya is on for the deep dive today. We received the stability logs you sent last night, Priya, thanks. Quick unpack and then model pinning discussion.

02:02 Priya: Cool, so tl;dr of the smoke runs: rwd-v2-small showed median latency around 130ms on your sample, p95 was 520ms, we did see two OOMs during a 12-hour burst test when seqLen spiked to 2k - likely KV cache pressure. rwd-v1-quant had higher latency (median ~210ms) but fewer memory spikes since quantization reduces footprint.

03:05 Emma: Wait, two OOMs? Can you repeat when that happened, was it on Dedicated or staging?
03:12 Priya: That was on our staging cluster with bswap config - so not Dedicated. I suspect config tweak (cache eviction threshold) will address it. Also quick note, the transcriptions that came in had some mislabels - the model names might appear as redwood-rwd2 in the export, ignore that.

04:00 Liam: How big is the delta in token cost between the two? If v2 is faster but hits OOMs, cost might spike with retries.

04:20 Jordan: We'll provide a cost delta table. Short answer: rwd-v2-small is slightly cheaper per token if it stays in-memory due to optimizations; but retries and longer tail latencies increase effective cost.

06:10 Alex: From security perspective, any differences in encryption/KMS when we move to Dedicated or Private? We need to know if the fallback flows still honor our HSM keys.
06:22 Priya: Good point. Fallback to hosted variants will respect the customer's KMS settings only if traffic remains within your private routing. If we fallback to siloed hosted model, you need to accept the host KMS - we can document that clearly and include the RBAC differences.

07:15 Emma: Our priority is correctness on clinical summarization tasks and predictable latency under 500ms for 95% of requests. Cost is secondary but important.

08:00 Priya: Right - from the evals we ran on your clinical prompts, rwd-v2-small had slightly better ROUGE/L and fewer hallucinations in the short summaries, rwd-v1-quant was more conservative but produced slightly shorter outputs (sometimes truncating). I'd recommend rwd-v2-small as primary with rwd-v1-quant as a pinned fallback variant.

09:12 Sam: Can the platform do automatic fallback (i.e., on OOM or p99 exceed) to the pinned fallback? Or do we need to route that in our app?

09:30 Priya: Redwood has both modes. You can configure automated fallback policy per route: failover on error type (OOM, timeout) or on latency SLO breach, and we can do seamless variant substitution. We'll show the config snippet.

11:05 Nora: For our CICD, we prefer a canary rollout with 5% traffic for 48h then 25% then full. Is that supported?
11:18 Jordan: Yes - canary with gradual ramp, and automatic rollback if model-level quality/regression monitors trigger. You can tie regressions to eval prompts so if F1 drops we rollback automatically.

12:40 Liam: On the regression monitors - we saw some small scoring drift in last week's run, was that because the model changed or because of prompt formatting?
12:52 Priya: Likely prompt formatting - there was an extra newline in your pipeline that changed tokenization. We normalized that in the latest runs. We'll attach diff.

14:10 Emma: About pinning: is pinning done at the model version level or at the artifact hash? We need immutable pinning for audits.
14:22 Priya: You can pin to exact model version ID (e.g., rwd-v2-small@2025-03-10-rc1) which is immutable. The UI will show model metadata and build hash; for audit we also emit model_version in the request logs.

16:00 Alex: Does audit log include fallback events (i.e., when automatic substitution happens)? We need to see which variant served each request.
16:10 Priya: Yes, every served response includes metadata: model_version, served_from (cache/dedicated/hosted), and fallback_reason if applicable. Those are stored in logs for your retention window.

18:00 Sam: For the fallback test we plan to mirror 10% of traffic to Redwood staging and trigger faults to validate rollback. Any tips?
18:15 Priya: Mirror to staging yes, and run an artificial mem-pressure job to emulate KV cache spikes. We'll provide scripts. Also, configure the policy for immediate fallback on OOM to reduce user-facing errors.

20:30 Jordan: Quick recap of numbers we saw: median 130ms for v2-small, p95 520ms with two OOMs in burst, v1-quant median 210ms p95 430ms no OOMs. Cost per token estimates, we'll circulate.

22:45 Emma: Does the quantized v1 have any QA/regulatory concerns? Sometimes quant models hallucinate more.
22:59 Priya: In our evals, v1-quant was more conservative here; hallucination rate was slightly higher on open-ended prompts, but on your templated clinical summarization it was okay. We should test on your exact prompts.

25:10 Liam: If we pin primary to rwd-v2-small and fallback to rwd-v1-quant, do we need to manage state (KV cache) migration between variants?
25:28 Priya: Cache isn't shared across model architectures. When we fallback the response completes on the fallback model; for long-running conversations KV cache differences can cause slightly different context handling. For your use-case (single-shot summarization) it's fine. For chat we can add prefix-preserving cache strategies but it's more complex.

27:00 Emma: OK. For acceptance criteria: p95 <= 500ms, no user-facing errors >0.1% in 7 days, and summary quality score >= baseline. Can you capture that as a checklist?
27:12 Jordan: Yep we'll formalize that.

29:00 Priya: Next technical items: I'll run a 24-hour stability test on rwd-v2-small with your max seqLen distribution; I'll increase cache eviction threshold and test again. I'll post the logs to the shared folder.

30:20 Sam: We'll provide the representative prompt sets and the 1k request test harness.

31:15 Jordan: On rollouts: recommend starting with pinned primary rwd-v2-small (canary 5% 48h), fallback to rwd-v1-quant on error/timeout, monitor eval prompts and latency SLOs, auto-rollback if regression triggered.

33:50 Nora: For Private deployment timing - if we move to Private later will those pinned versions maintain the same hashes? Are there build differences?
34:05 Priya: We keep identical artifacts across environments; build hash is reproducible, but quantization builds can differ slightly if you use different hardware. We'll note that in the migration doc.

35:40 Emma: Anything else from security? Alex?
35:45 Alex: Just need to review the fallback trace flow to ensure no sensitive PHI is logged in hosted fallbacks. We'll want a config that redacts PHI before logs leave the VPC.
35:58 Priya: We can add a pre-logging redact hook and consult on DLP patterns.

37:20 Jordan: Alright, quick recap of next steps and owners - Priya does the stability run and sends plan, Emma provides prompts, Sam sets up mirroring, Jordan sends pricing and rollback doc. We'll schedule the Private deep-dive separately. Anything else?
37:40 Emma: Nope that covers it. Thanks.

38:00 Jordan: Thanks everyone, adjourn.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mislabels (redwood-rwd2, rwd-v1-quant sometimes appears as rwd1q). There was brief cross-talk at 00:09-00:13.

End of transcript.
